prompt: We're running a distributed rate limiter that enforces per-client limits with a sliding-window log: for every client we keep one Redis sorted-set entry per request (member = request id, score = timestamp), and each admission check evicts entries older than the window and counts what's left. It's exact and correct, but in production the hottest clients — the ones sending the most traffic — are blowing up Redis memory and CPU, because RAM grows linearly with in-window request volume and the eviction-plus-count cost lands on exactly the keys already under the heaviest load. Below is the current `SlidingWindowLogLimiter`. Optimize the memory and per-operation cost of the hot path for a client that only needs limiting (not exact accounting) — walk me through your replacement, what you give up to get it, and how you'd verify the swap is safe before shipping it to production.
